issue_context.title: Polars fails to recognize the benefits of an already sorted rle_id()
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl
import numpy as np

# Number of rows and groups
num_rows = 1_000_000
num_groups = 200

np.random.seed(123)

random_numbers = np.random.rand(num_rows)

groups = np.random.choice(range(num_groups), num_rows)

# Create a Polars DataFrame
df = pl.DataFrame({
    "Groups": groups,
    "RandomNumbers": random_numbers
})

df = df.with_columns(pl.col("RandomNumbers").rle_id().alias("ID"))

%timeit df.with_columns(pl.col("RandomNumbers").last().over("ID"))

df=df.sort("ID")

%timeit df.with_columns(pl.col("RandomNumbers").last().over("ID"))


```


### Log output

```shell
110 ms ± 8.13 ms per loop (mean ± std. dev. of 7 runs, 10 loops each)
4.59 ms ± 186 µs per loop (mean ± std. dev. of 7 runs, 100 loops each)
```

### Issue description

So sometimes by sorting the dataframe prehand some functions becomes way faster. However, it seems like polars is not able to recognize that rle_id() is already sorted. By sorting by "ID" the last line of code becomes over 20x faster. However, the first line of code before sorting should also be equally as fast as rle_id() is already sorted. Am I missing something? If not, it would be nice of someone could find a fix to this

### Expected behavior

That the two line of codes are equally as fast

comments:
A different way to show the issue is

```
pl.select(pl.Series('a',[1,2,3])).with_columns(b=pl.col('a').rle_id())['b'].flags

{'SORTED_ASC': False, 'SORTED_DESC': False}
```

In the mean time, you can do 
```
pl.select(pl.Series('a',[1,2,3])).with_columns(b=pl.col('a').rle_id().set_sorted())['b'].flags
```
